title: Index one and residue separability survive normalized finite base change
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension], satisfying $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and with separable residue field extension $(B/\mathfrak m_B)/(A/\mathfrak m_A)$ in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. For a finite field extension $N/K$, let $R$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $N$ and $C$ the integral closure of $B$ in $E=(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every maximal ideal $q$ of $C$, $n=q\cap R$ is maximal, $R_n$ and $C_q$ are discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $nC_q=qC_q$, and $\kappa(q)/\kappa(n)$ is separable. These local assertions require no essential finite type, completeness, or separability of $N/K$. If, in addition, the tensor algebra $T=B\otimes_AR$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], then $L\otimes_KN$ is reduced and the canonical map $T\to C$ is an isomorphism. Finite means finite-dimensional; reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent element; local means pulling back maximal ideals to maximal ideals.

source.place: Tag 09EQ, lemma-formally-smooth-goes-up, expressed by the equivalent index-one and separable-residue criterion Tag 09E7 (lemma-extension-dvrs-formally-smooth); Tag 09EM (remark-construction) supplies the localizations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a) with $P=N$. It gives that $n=q\cap R$ is maximal, $V=R_n$ and $D=C_q$ are DVRs, and $k_n=\kappa(n)$ is finite over $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Put $F=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Choose uniformizers $\pi\in A$ and $t\in V$. The canonical maps $V\to D$ and $B\to D$ are injective and local: the embeddings of the fields $N,L$ into the field factor of $E$ selected by $q$ give injectivity; contraction gives locality. In particular $t$ has nonzero image in the maximal ideal of $D$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (1),(3), via case (a) of the cited structure statement

proof.text: Let $U=B\otimes_A V$, let $p$ be the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $D$ under $U\to D$, and put $S=U_p$. This map extends to a local map $\phi:S\to D$ because every element outside $p$ maps to a unit. As $\pi\in tV$ and $\pi B=\mathfrak m_B$, balancing pure tensors gives $U/tU\cong F\otimes_k k_n$, sending $b\otimes v$ to $\bar b\otimes\bar v$; its inverse sends residue tensors to the classes of lifts. Thus $S/tS$ is a prime localization of $F\otimes_k k_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-residue-finite-tensor-fields]: this is a field $H$ separable over $k_n$. Consequently the maximal ideal of $S$ is exactly $tS$. No Noetherianity of $S$ is inferred.

source.place: Tag 09EQ, lemma-formally-smooth-goes-up, displayed closed-fibre calculation; valid local part only

proof.text: Write $E_0$ for the field factor of $E$ selected by $q$. The image of $C$ in $E_0$ has fraction field $E_0$: for $x\in E_0$, a monic polynomial over $L$ for $x$ becomes a monic polynomial over $B$ for $\pi^a x$ when $a$ clears its finitely many denominators; the factor idempotents are integral as well. Hence $\operatorname{Frac}(D)=E_0$. Likewise $R[1/\pi]=N$ by scaling a monic polynomial over $K$, and $B[1/\pi]=L$. Therefore the image of $U[1/\pi]$ in $E_0$ is the whole field $E_0$, since the projection $L\otimes_KN\to E_0$ is onto. It follows that the subring $I=\phi(S)\subset D$ has fraction field $E_0$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction, generic localization identity; denominator scaling written out

proof.text: Use the integer valuation $v_D$ of the DVR $D$. For $x\in S$ with $\phi(x)\ne0$, membership $x\in t^rS$ implies $v_D(\phi(x))\ge r v_D(t)$, so there is a largest such $r$. Write $x=t^ru$; maximality gives $u\notin tS$, hence $u$ is a unit. Thus every nonzero element of $I$ is $t^r$ times a unit of $I$. By Step 3, every nonzero element of $D\subset\operatorname{Frac}(I)$ is $t^m$ times a unit of $I$ for some integer $m$; its nonnegative $D$-valuation forces $m\ge0$. Hence $\phi$ is onto. Also $\ker\phi=\bigcap_{r\ge0}t^rS$: the intersection maps to zero by the same valuation bound, whereas any element outside it is $t^r$ times a unit and has nonzero image. This argument uses only the valuation description of a DVR, not a Noetherian principal-ideal criterion for $S$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, valuation description; direct argument repairing the Noetherianity gap in 09EQ

proof.text: The image of $t$ generates the maximal ideal of $D$. Indeed surjectivity of $\phi$ and its locality give $\mathfrak m_D=\phi(tS)=tD$. Since $nV=tV$, this is $nD=qD$. Moreover $\ker\phi\subset tS$, so the induced residue map $S/tS\to D/tD$ is an isomorphism. The isomorphisms in Step 2 preserve the structural $k_n$-map, and thus identify $\kappa(q)/\kappa(n)$ with $H/k_n$, which is separable. This proves every unconditional local assertion.

source.place: Tag 09E7, lemma-extension-dvrs-formally-smooth, index-one and residue-separability meaning; quotient calculation from Steps 2 and 4

proof.text: For the additional global assertion assume $T$ is Noetherian. The injective map $A\to B$ makes $B$ torsion free over the PID $A$, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring $R\hookrightarrow N$ with $B$ remains injective. In $B\otimes_AN$, $\pi$ is invertible; it is therefore a nonzerodivisor on $T$. The identities of Step 3 give $T[1/\pi]=L\otimes_KN$. The kernel of $T\to C$ is exactly the nilradical: after inverting $\pi$ it is the kernel of reduction to $E$, so each kernel element has a nilpotent power killed by a power of $\pi$, hence is nilpotent; nilpotents map to zero in $C$. Since every element of $C$ is integral over $B$, it is integral over $T$ too. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] to $T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow C$ to lift every prime of $T$ to $C$.

source.place: Tags 0AUW and 00GQ, PID flatness and integral lying over; the source 09EQ comparison repaired with the missing Noetherianity hypothesis

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $p$ of $T$ and choose a prime $q$ of $C$ over it by Step 6. It is maximal: the domain $C/q$ is integral over the field $T/p$, so for a nonzero element its monic minimal polynomial has nonzero constant coefficient and expresses its inverse. The contraction $n=q\cap R$ is maximal by the structure statement in Step 1. Localizing first at $R\setminus n$ and then at $p$ identifies $T_p$ with the ring $S$ of Step 2. It is now Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with ring $S$, ideal $tS=\mathfrak m_S$, and finite module $S$ over itself. Its intersection of powers is zero; Step 4 therefore makes $T_p\to C_q$ an isomorphism. In particular every maximal localization of $T$ is a DVR. Every prime localization is a localization of one of these DVRs, hence either that DVR or its fraction field (a DVR has only the primes zero and its maximal ideal). These are integrally closed by their valuation descriptions, so $T$ is normal in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (2); Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; Tag 00GV, definition-ring-normal

proof.text: The kernel of $T\to C$ localizes to zero at every maximal ideal by Step 7, hence is zero: a nonzero kernel element has a proper annihilator, contained in some maximal ideal, at which it cannot vanish. Thus localizing the injection identifies $T[1/\pi]=L\otimes_KN$ with $E=C[1/\pi]$, so the former is reduced. Furthermore $E$ is the total fraction ring of $T$. Indeed it is already a localization at the nonzerodivisor $\pi$, and any nonzerodivisor $s\in T$ has nonzero projection to every field factor of $E$: otherwise the corresponding nonzero idempotent, multiplied by a power of $\pi$ to lie in $T$, would annihilate $s$. Thus $s$ is a unit of $E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] to the normal ring $T$. Every $c\in C\subset E$ is integral over $B\subset T$, hence integral over $T$ and belongs to $T$. Therefore $T\to C$ is also surjective, giving the claimed comparison isomorphism under the stated extra hypothesis.
